text.p: - The Russian cabinet has discussed a draft law introducing a new tax to be levied on individuals and merchandise at each Russian border crossing and concluded that it has to be amended.
- Moscow has cut the number of city casinos from 137 to 33 in 1996 and is planning to reduce it eventually to just five.
- The Finance Ministry and Central Bank plan to put an end to surrogate money widely used by cash-strapped local administrations and ailing enterprises across Russia.

- Russia will try to negotiate a deal with NATO regarding its eastwards expansion and will not take any retaliatory measures before alliance forces set foot on the territory of Russia's former allies.
- Russia has to strengthen its state structures to make it possible for the economy to crawl out of recession.
- The price of strong spirits in 1997 will not rise more than 20 percent in the wake of a clamp-down on illegal production and cheap imports.
- Experts in the Russian Mint research institute are working on a new half-paper, half-plastic money supposed to be put in circulation in the next century.
